Bike vs Car in Rush Hour: How Much Faster Are You Really?

2026-09-22 Bicycling.nl TomTom, Traffic Index, Amsterdam, cycling, e-bike, race bike, car, rush hour, urban mobility, congestion, Netherlands, commuting, speed comparison
Read the source article

Quick summary

Using TomTom Traffic Index data, Bicycling.nl demonstrates that in Amsterdam's evening rush hour a car travels at the same speed as an e-bike (about 22 km/h), making the bicycle the faster option for urban trips under 10 km — especially once parking time is factored in.

Key takeaways

  • Amsterdam is the slowest car city in the Netherlands: cars average less than 23 km/h, and in the evening rush hour a 10-km trip takes 27 minutes (about 22 km/h)
  • An e-bike travels at 20–25 km/h, meaning in Amsterdam's evening rush hour a car is no faster than an e-bike
  • A race bike at 23–27 km/h in city traffic is faster than a car in rush hour, even before parking time is considered
  • On distances under 5 km in the city, the bicycle is virtually always faster than a car once parking is accounted for
  • The crossover point depends on the city: in Nijmegen, where cars average over 28 km/h, even an e-bike is slower over 10 km
  • Amsterdam car commuters lost 97 hours per year to traffic in 2025 according to TomTom — more than four full days
  • A University of Utrecht study found that cycling 75 minutes per week extends life by about half a year
